newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Armenian court considers election challenge.
newsitem.headline: Armenian court considers election challenge.

text.p: Armenia's Constitutional Court began deliberating on Thursday whether to annul the results of a presidential election two months ago in which incumbent Levon Ter-Petrosyan won a second five-year term.
Former prime minister Vazgen Manukyan, who challenged Ter-Petrosyan in the September 22 election, has accused the president of vote-rigging.
Ter-Petrosyan, a Soviet-era dissident and former close ally of Manukyan in the independence cause, denies the charge.

Manukyan has said he doubts that the court, composed of judges appointed by the president and a parliament dominated by the president's bloc, will rule in his favour. The court is due to give its verdict by November 24.

Foreign observers noted major irregularities by Ter-Petrosyan forces, and the Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) said they could have been serious enough to call his victory into question.
Manukyan's representative said figures from the Central Electoral Commission, which is defending the election, were wrong by tens of thousands of votes.

The Central Electoral Commission says Ter-Petrosyan, officially sworn in on November 11, won with 51.8 percent of the votes, just clearing the 50-percent hurdle needed to win without a run-off. It said Manukyan won 41.3 percent.
